source_basis.ownership_note: Canonical operating cost rates and direct cost assumptions. Runtime outputs should supply quantities; this file supplies cost rates.

rate.assumption_note: Need real feed purchase cost, delivered basis, and feed type.
Need fingerling purchase basis and whether freight/mortality-in-transit is included.

records.notes: Kept separate from feed because it behaves like a batch input rather than a daily operating cost.

rate.assumption_note: Need site tariff, tax treatment, and whether demand charges are excluded or modeled elsewhere.

records.notes: Can later be expanded to time-of-use pricing if necessary.

rate.assumption_note: Need site water/sewer treatment basis and whether discharge costs apply. Upstream/runtime water use may still arrive as liters and should be normalized to m3 before applying this rate.

records.notes: Canonical business rate uses currency_per_m3. Current upstream/runtime water-use examples may still expose water_use_l and should be converted at the mapping boundary.

rate.assumption_note: Need explicit basis: seed, seedling, plug, or transplants.

records.notes: Use only after the project chooses the canonical planting input basis.
records.schema_choice_note: Choose one canonical planting-input basis before population so cost basis is explicit in both unit and sourcing assumptions.

rate.assumption_note: Need explicit basis: seed, seedling, or propagated transplant.

records.notes: Kept parallel to lettuce for simpler first-pass cost modeling.
records.schema_choice_note: Choose one canonical planting-input basis before population so cost basis is explicit in both unit and sourcing assumptions.

rate.assumption_note: Need a canonical supplement costing basis before populating a numeric rate.

records.notes: Included because existing knowledge already highlights buffering and supplementation as operationally important.
records.schema_choice_note: Choose one canonical supplement driver basis before promotion and align the rate unit to that basis.

rate.assumption_note: Need canonical packaging basis after sale unit is fixed by channel.

records.notes: Kept unit-flexible until the project decides whether lettuce is billed primarily by head or kg.
records.schema_choice_note: Choose one canonical packaging driver basis before promotion and align the rate unit to that basis.

rate.assumption_note: Need canonical packaging basis after sale unit is fixed by channel.

records.notes: Separated from channel assumptions because physical packing cost is a direct operating input, but kept optional until basil sale-unit basis is fixed.
records.schema_choice_note: Choose one canonical packaging driver basis before promotion and align the rate unit to that basis.
records.activation_note: Keep deferred until basil packaging is tied to one canonical sale-unit basis.

rate.assumption_note: Need a canonical changeover-cleaning cost basis before populating a numeric rate.

records.notes: Use for media-bed root clean-out and between-crop reset work, especially where short-cycle greens create frequent changeovers.
records.schema_choice_note: Choose whether media-bed changeover cleaning is modeled per crop turn, per grow area, or per planting-site basis before promotion.

rate.assumption_note: Need a canonical media-washing cost basis before populating a numeric rate.

records.notes: Use for periodic gravel or media washing when solids loading or clogging pushes media beds beyond routine changeover cleaning.
records.schema_choice_note: Choose whether gravel or media washing is modeled per maintenance event, per media volume, or per grow area before promotion.

rate.assumption_note: Need a canonical raft-cleaning and foam-replacement cost basis before populating a numeric rate.

records.notes: Use for raft-surface cleaning, raft wear, and related consumable replacement in DWC or raft crop programs.
records.schema_choice_note: Choose whether raft cleaning and foam replacement is modeled per crop turn, per grow area, or per raft panel before promotion.

rate.assumption_note: Need a canonical channel-sanitation cost basis before populating a numeric rate.

records.notes: Use for between-crop NFT channel sanitation so architecture-specific hygiene work is not hidden inside a generic maintenance bucket.
records.schema_choice_note: Choose whether NFT channel sanitation is modeled per crop turn, per channel length, or per planting-site basis before promotion.

rate.assumption_note: Need a canonical unclogging and filter-service cost basis before populating a numeric rate.

records.notes: Use as a first-pass hybrid bucket for NFT channel-side unclogging and related upstream filter-service burden, where cleaner-water dependence and orifice reliability make both intrinsic and amplified maintenance business-relevant.
records.schema_choice_note: Keep event-driven channel service and support-system filter service explicit. If later split, drive channel-side work by service event or channel_length_m and drive upstream filter service by design flow or feed load.

rate.assumption_note: Need a canonical solids-removal operating-cost basis before populating a numeric rate.

records.notes: Use for explicit solids-removal operating burden in architectures that depend on cleaner upstream water, especially DWC or raft and NFT configurations.
records.schema_choice_note: Choose whether solids-removal operations are modeled per operating day, per feed load, or per design-flow basis before promotion.

rate.assumption_note: Need a canonical backup-power operating-cost basis before populating a numeric rate.

records.notes: Use for generator fuel, routine testing, or standby service. The category is system-wide, but its business importance is highest where outage sensitivity is fastest, especially NFT.
records.schema_choice_note: Choose whether backup-power mitigation is modeled per operating day, per equipment runtime hour, or per test event before promotion.
